body:
That 'something's still missing' feeling after hanging art?


 I hear it constantly. 
The room looks tidy but not quite alive.
😔

Almost every time, 
the fix is layering — starting with one anchor piece and building outward with different sizes, heights, and shapes.


 It sounds technical, but honestly it's closer to getting dressed than doing a maths problem.
I wrote this guide to walk you through exactly how I approach it — anchor first, then supporting pieces, then the small accents that make a wall feel genuinely considered rather than accidental.

If you fancy experimenting with your own layout before committing to anything,

close: Once you see how layering works, your walls become the simplest, lowest-risk place to start building a room you actually love.
I'd love to know — do you have an anchor piece already, or are you starting from scratch?
Hit reply — I read every one.

title: How to Choose Your Interior Design Style
subject: {{ first_name|title|default:'Friend' }}, not sure where to start with your decor?

copy.subject: {{ first_name|title|default:'Friend' }}, not sure where to start with your decor?
copy.preview: Before you buy a single thing, you may want to read this first.
body:
That moment when you're standing in a shop (or staring at your cart) thinking: 
'Do I actually like this, or am I just guessing?' — I hear it constantly.
❤️

The truth is, most people start buying pieces they like before they've worked out what they're actually going for.


Which is how you may end up with pieces you individually love but that never quite click together. 
 I wrote a guide that walks you through how to spot your own style before you spend a penny — so that when you do choose wall art, it feels right straight away rather than 'maybe'.

primaryButton.label: READ THE GUIDE & FIND YOUR STYLE

close: Once you know your style, wall art is honestly the easiest — and lowest-risk — place to bring it to life first.
What's making you hesitate most right now — colour, size, or just not knowing where to begin?
Hit reply — I read every one.
